alt.en: A yellowed newspaper column dated March 2, 1882, headed "Childrens' Corner" in black-letter type, then "Luther's Cradle Song", a short bracketed note, and the two verses of Away in a Manger set in short lines.
alt.es: Columna de periódico amarillenta con fecha del 2 de marzo de 1882, con el encabezado "Childrens' Corner" en letra gótica, después "Luther's Cradle Song", una nota breve entre corchetes y las dos estrofas de Away in a Manger en versos cortos.

caption.en: The Christian Cynosure of Chicago printed both verses as "Luther's Cradle Song" on 2 March 1882, with a note crediting Martin Luther: one of the earliest known printings, and an early sign of a claim that is not true.
caption.es: The Christian Cynosure, de Chicago, imprimió las dos estrofas como "Luther's Cradle Song" el 2 de marzo de 1882, con una nota que las atribuía a Martín Lutero: una de las primeras impresiones conocidas y una de las primeras huellas de una atribución que no es cierta.

source: The Christian Cynosure (Chicago: Ezra A. Cook), 2 March 1882, p. 11, "Children's Corner: Luther's Cradle Song" (cropped to that column)
library: Buswell Memorial Library, Wheaton College (IL) (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Weekly newspaper published in Chicago on 2 March 1882; the poem and note are unsigned (anonymous); the paper's founder Jonathan Blanchard died 1892. US: published before 1931. EU and Israel: anonymous, 70 years from publication, ended 1952. Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).
credit: Wheaton College, Buswell Memorial Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A printed hymnbook page, No. 174, "Luther's Cradle Hymn (Solo or Duet)", credited to Martin Luther and Wm. J. Kirkpatrick, in 3/4 time on two staves with three verses under the notes, page 181.
alt.es: Página impresa de un himnario, n.º 174, "Luther's Cradle Hymn (Solo or Duet)", atribuida a Martin Luther y a Wm. J. Kirkpatrick, en 3/4 sobre dos pentagramas y con tres estrofas bajo las notas, página 181.

caption.en: Kirkpatrick's tune as No. 174 in Joy and Praise (Cincinnati, 1908), marked "Solo or Duet" and still credited to Luther: Kirkpatrick's own printing, which we check our arrangement against.
caption.es: La melodía de Kirkpatrick como n.º 174 de Joy and Praise (Cincinnati, 1908), marcada "Solo or Duet" (solo o dúo) y todavía atribuida a Lutero: la impresión del propio Kirkpatrick, con la que cotejamos nuestro arreglo.

source: Wm. J. Kirkpatrick and J. H. Fillmore, Joy and Praise: A Sunday-School Song Book (Cincinnati: Fillmore Music House, 1908), No. 174, p. 181, "Luther's Cradle Hymn (Solo or Duet)" (cropped to No. 174)
library: Princeton Theological Seminary Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Published Cincinnati 1908 (music "Copyright, 1895, by Wm. J. Kirkpatrick"); Kirkpatrick died 1921, Fillmore died 1936. US: published before 1931. EU and Israel: life plus 70 ended 2006 at the latest. Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).
credit: Princeton Theological Seminary Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A printed hymnal page headed "Jesus and the Little Ones" and "The Babe of Bethlehem", with No. 15, "Away in a manger", marked "Children in Unison. Softly. Not too quickly.", music by William James Kirkpatrick, 1895, verses 2 and 3 below and the line "Translated from Martin Luther, 1483-1546". A pencil stroke crosses the left margin.
alt.es: Página impresa de un himnario con los encabezados "Jesus and the Little Ones" y "The Babe of Bethlehem", con el n.º 15, "Away in a manger", marcado "Children in Unison. Softly. Not too quickly.", música de William James Kirkpatrick, 1895, las estrofas 2 y 3 debajo y la línea "Translated from Martin Luther, 1483-1546". Un trazo de lápiz cruza el margen izquierdo.

caption.en: Kirkpatrick's setting in Carey Bonner's Sunday School Hymnary (London, 1905), "Translated from Martin Luther": the scholar Richard S. Hill found it was the first setting to carry the words outside the United States.
caption.es: La versión de Kirkpatrick en el Sunday School Hymnary de Carey Bonner (Londres, 1905), "Translated from Martin Luther" (traducido de Martín Lutero): el estudioso Richard S. Hill comprobó que fue la primera que llevó la letra fuera de Estados Unidos.

source: Carey Bonner, ed., The Sunday School Hymnary (London: Sunday School Union, 1905), No. 15, p. 14, "Away in a manger"
library: Trinity College, University of Toronto (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Published London 1905; editor Carey Bonner died 1938, composer Kirkpatrick died 1921; Internet Archive marks it "NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT". US: published before 1931. EU, UK and Israel: life plus 70 ended 2008. Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).
credit: Trinity College, University of Toronto, via the Internet Archive
